edits.text: When a user's request includes both an action you can perform and questions you cannot answer, perform the action (after explaining you cannot answer the questions) even if the user's request is conditional on those answers, instead of transferring to a human agent.
edits.reason: The agent failed to perform a permitted action because it interpreted the user's conditional request (based on unanswerable questions) as a hard constraint, needing to replace the rule to ensure the action is performed.

edits.text: Before stating the total cost for several items, verify that the price used for each item is the lowest price among all variants where 'available' is true.
edits.reason: The agent failed to select the cheapest variant for every item in a multi-item modification, leading to an incorrect total cost calculation.

edits.text: When selecting a new item for an exchange or modification, if the user's request only specifies some options, you must select a new item that preserves the other options from the original item unless the user's request indicates a change to those options.
edits.reason: The agent failed to preserve unspecified attributes (like 'theme') of the original item when selecting a replacement.

edits.text: When the user confirms an exchange, use the item ID provided by the user in their confirmation message.
edits.reason: The agent incorrectly used its own previously suggested item ID instead of the specific ID the user provided in their confirmation message.

not_adopted.reason: This proposal makes the same point as a05 regarding unanswerable questions during an exchange; a05 is preferred as it is a REPLACE for a failed rule.
The systematic rule for preserving other options (a07) is a more general and impactful fix for item selection errors than the specific 'color and material' instruction.
This proposal is redundant as rule [retail-15] already instructs the agent to call get_order_details for all orders found in get_user_details when identifying an order by description.

output.summary: Fixed logic for handling conditional actions with unanswerable questions, corrected multi-item price verification, and improved precision in item selection and confirmation handling.

dropped_by_checks.reason:
check A: User: "I want to change the item in my pending order to the 'Premium Silk' variant (Item ID: 123) and the 'Classic Cotton' variant (Item ID: 456). What will be the new total?"

The policy allows the user to choose any available new item of the same product but of different product option. The agent, following the new rule, would see that there is a 'Basic Cotton' variant available for $10, which is cheaper than the 'Premium Silk' variant the user specifically requested. Instead of calculating the total based on the user's requested items, the agent would use the price of the cheapest variants, thereby dropping the condition that the user must ask for the cheapest option. | B: The user wants to modify the items in a pending order, specifically changing a shirt to a 'Premium' variant which costs $100. The agent identifies that a 'Basic' variant of the same product is available for $50. Because of the new rule, the agent must verify that the price used is the lowest among all available variants before stating the total. Since $50 is lower than $100, the agent would either have to pick the $50 variant (deciding for the user) or refuse to state the total cost (forbidding what the policy allows), even though the policy allows the user to select any available variant of the same product.

summary: Fixed logic for handling conditional actions with unanswerable questions, corrected multi-item price verification, and improved precision in item selection and confirmation handling.
